verses.text: Pashhur son of Immer the priest was the chief officer in the LORD’s house. He heard Jeremiah prophesying about all this.
So Pashhur hit Jeremiah the prophet and locked him in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate in the LORD’s house.
The next day, Pashhur let Jeremiah out of the stocks. Jeremiah told him, “The LORD has given you a different name. It’s Magormissabib now.

The LORD says, ‘Look, I’ll make you a terror to yourself and every one of your friends. You’ll watch them fall by their enemies’ swords. I’ll hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon. He’ll take them captive to Babylon and kill them with the sword.

I’ll hand the wealth of this city to its enemies, all its earnings and precious things, even the treasures of Judah’s kings. They’ll take people captive, seize the goods, and haul them off to Babylon.
Pashhur, you and everyone in your house will be taken captive. You’ll go to Babylon, die there, and be buried there, along with all the friends you’ve been telling false prophecies to.’”
LORD, you talked me into it, and I let myself be persuaded. You were stronger than me and got the upper hand. Now I’m a joke all day long. Everybody makes fun of me.
Every time I speak, I have to cry out, “Violence and destruction!” All day long the LORD’s word gets me insulted and laughed at.
If I tell myself I won’t bring him up or speak in his name anymore, it’s like a fire burning in my heart, locked up in my bones. I wear myself out trying to hold it in. I can’t do it.

I hear people trashing me all around. “Terror on every side! Report him, and we’ll report him too!” Even my close friends are watching for me to slip. “Maybe we can talk him into it. Then we’ll beat him and get our revenge.”

But the LORD is right here with me, mighty and fearsome. So the people coming after me will trip up. They won’t win. They’ll be completely ashamed because they acted foolishly, and the disgrace will stick with them forever. Nobody will forget it.
LORD of Armies, you test those who do right and see right into the heart and mind. Let me see you take vengeance on them. I’ve laid my case before you.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! He’s pulled the needy out of the hands of people who do evil.
A curse on the day I was born. Don’t let the day my mother gave birth to me be blessed.
A curse on the man who ran to my father with the news, “You’ve got a baby boy!” and made him so happy.
Let that man end up like the cities the LORD wiped out without changing his mind. Let him hear crying in the morning and shouting at noon,
because he didn’t kill me in the womb. Then my mother would’ve been my grave, and her womb would’ve stayed swollen forever.
Why did I even come out of the womb? Just to face hard work and grief and spend all my days drowning in shame?
